assessments.reasoning: Printed I-37 §3.6.10 identifies the glvn argument as Selective Kill. Killing the named variable makes its value undefined and includes every longer matching-prefix subscript tuple. The unrestricted suffix set for an unsubscripted target follows from the same-name rule.

challenge.method: Compare killing a subscripted leaf, a branch with children, an unsubscripted root, an already zero-data target, and a neighboring same-name branch. Read the argumentless and exclusive local forms alongside the vendor’s separately documented ZKILL.
challenge.results: Selective KILL acts on the named target and every descendant on its branch. A sibling with a different prefix and an untouched ancestor remain outside the killed subtree. The already-zero case has no effect. The argumentless and exclusive forms operate on local variables in the distinct ways stated, and the vendor extension ZKILL is scoped to clearing a node value while preserving descendants.

limitations: The verdict is confined to the 1975 selective named-variable form. The historical ancestor’s $DATA treatment and reinstatement after SET have their own clauses.
